questions.question: Given a vector field \(F=y^{2}xa_{x}-yza_{y}-x^{2}a_{z}\), the line integral \(\int F\cdot dl\) evaluated along a segment on the x-axis from x = 1 to x = 2 is
questions.explanation:
To find: \(\int \vec{F}\cdot \vec{dl}\) along a segment on the x-axis from x=1 and x=2.
i.e. Y=0, z=0, dy=0 and dz=0
\[\begin{aligned} \int \vec{F}\cdot \vec{dl}&= \int (y^2 \times \hat{a_x}-yz\hat{a_y}-x^2\hat{a_z})(\hat{a_x}dx +\hat{a_y}dy+\hat{a_z}dz)\\ &= \int y^2x \;dx-yz\; dy -x^2 \; dz \end{aligned}\]
Putting y=0, z=0, dy=0 and dz=0, we get \(\int \vec{F}\cdot \vec{dl}=0\)

questions.subject: electric-circuits
questions.question: Three capacitors \(C_1, C_2 \; and \; C_3\) whose values are 10 \(\mu\)F, 5 \(\mu\)F, and 2 \(\mu\)F respectively, have breakdown voltages of 10 V, 5 V and 2 V respectively. For the interconnection shown below, the maximum safe voltage in Volts that can be applied across the combination, and the corresponding total charge in \(\mu\)C stored in the effective capacitance across the terminals are respectively,
questions.explanation:
\(Q=CV\)
\(Q_1=C_1V_1 =10 \times 10^{-6} \times 10=100\mu C\)
\(Q_2=C_2V_2 =5 \times 10^{-6} \times 5=25\mu C\)
\(Q_3=C_3V_3 =2 \times 10^{-6} \times 2=4\mu C\)
Capacitor \(C_2 \; and \; C_3\) are in series.
In series charge is same.
So, maximum charge on \(C_2 \; and \; C_3\) will be minimum of
\((Q_2,Q_3)=min(25\mu C,4\mu C)=4\mu C=Q_{23}\).
In series the equivalent capacitance of \(C_2 \; and \; C_3\) is
\(C_{23}=\frac{C_2C_3}{C_2+C_3}=\frac{5 \times 2}{5+2}=\frac{10}{7}\mu F\)
So, equivalent voltage,
\(V_{23}=\frac{Q_{23}}{C_{23}}=\frac{4 \times 10^{-6}}{\frac{10}{7} \times 10^{-6}}=\frac{28}{10}2.8V\)
In parallel, the voltage is same.
\(V_1=V_{23}=2.8V\)
Change in capacitor \(C_1\)
\(Q_1=C_1V_1 =10 \times 10^{-6}\times 2.8=28\mu C\)
In parallel, the total charge
\(Q=Q_1+Q_{23}\)
\(Q=4+28=32\mu C\)

questions.question: A Matrix has eigenvalues -1 and -2. The corresponding eigenvectors are \[\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -1 \end{bmatrix} and \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -2 \end{bmatrix}\] respectively. The matrix is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} AX &=\lambda X \\ \begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ c & d \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -1 \end{bmatrix}&=(-1) \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\\ a-b&= -1\\ c-d&=1 \\ \begin{bmatrix} a & b\;\;...(i)\\ c & d\;\;...(ii) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -2 \end{bmatrix}&=(-2) \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -2 \end{bmatrix}\\ a-2b&=-2\;\;...(iii) \\ c-2d&=4\;\;...(iv) \end{aligned}\]
From equation (i) and (iii), a=0 and b=1
From equation (ii) and (iv), c=-2 and d=-3
\[A= \begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ c & d \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\]

questions.question:
In the figure shown below, the chopper feeds a resistive load from a battery source. MOSFET Q is switched at 250 kHz, with a duty ratio of 0.4. All elements of the circuit are assumed to be ideal.

The average source current in Amps in steady-state is
questions.explanation:
As it is a boost converter, average current through capacitor is zero.
When Q is ON, \(I_c=-I_0\)
\(I_c=I_s-I_0\)
Therefore, average through capacitor
\[\begin{aligned} &=(-I_0)I_{ON}+(I_s-I_0)T_{OFF}=0 \\ &(-I_0)DT+(I_s-I_0)(1-D)T=0 \\ & -I_0D+I_s-I_sD-I_0+I_0D=0\\ &\Rightarrow \;\; I_0=(1-D)I_s\\ I_s&=\frac{I_0}{(1-D)}\\ &=\frac{V_0}{R(1-D)}\\ &=\frac{V_s}{R(1-D)^2}\\ &=\frac{12}{20(1-0.4)^2}=\frac{5}{3}A \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
In the figure shown below, the chopper feeds a resistive load from a battery source. MOSFET Q is switched at 250 kHz, with a duty ratio of 0.4. All elements of the circuit are assumed to be ideal.

The PEAK-TO-PEAK source current ripple in Amps is
questions.explanation:
Here,
\[\begin{aligned} I_{source}&=\text{Inductor current}\\ \because \;\; V&=L\frac{dI_s}{dt}\\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{V}{L}\int_{0}^{T_{ON}}dt&=\int_{min}^{max}dI_s\\ \Rightarrow \;\frac{V}{L}T_{ON}&=I_{s\; max}-I_{s \; min}\\ &= \text{ripple source current}\\ \Rightarrow \; T_{ON}&=D.T.\\ \therefore \; \text{ripple source current}&=\frac{V}{L}(D.T.)\\ &=\frac{12}{100 \times 10^{-6}}\times 0.4 \times \frac{1}{250 \times 10^3}\\ &=0.192A \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
The state variable formulation of a system is given as
\[\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x_1}\\ \dot{x_2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0\\ 0&-1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\1 \end{bmatrix}u\] \[x_1(0)=0,x_2(0)=0\ and \; y=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}\]
The system is
options: both not controllable and not observable
questions.explanation:
\[A= egin{bmatrix} -2 &0 \ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix},\] \[B= egin{bmatrix} 1\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[AB= egin{bmatrix} -2 &0 \ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix} egin{bmatrix} 1\ 1 \end{bmatrix}= egin{bmatrix} -2\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\]
For controllability, \(|B \; : \;\;AB| eq 0\)
\[\;\;\; egin{bmatrix} 1 & -2\ 1& -1 \end{bmatrix}=-1-(-2)=1 eq 0\]
The system is controllable.
\[C^T= egin{bmatrix} 1\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[A^TC^T= egin{bmatrix} -2 &0 \ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix} egin{bmatrix} 1\ 0 \end{bmatrix}= egin{bmatrix} -2\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
For observability, \([C^T\;: \; A^TC^T] eq 0\)
\[ egin{bmatrix} 1 & -2\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}=0\]
The system is not observable.

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question:
The state variable formulation of a system is given as
\[\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x_1}\\ \dot{x_2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0\\ 0&-1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\1 \end{bmatrix}u\] \[x_1(0)=0,x_2(0)=0\ and \; y=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}\]
The response y(t) to the unit step input is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} [sI-A]&=\begin{bmatrix} s & 0\\ 0 &s \end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0\\ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} s+2 & 0\\ 0 &s+1 \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2} & 0\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}[B]&=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2} & 0\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2}\\ \frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix} \\ C[sI-A]^{-1}[B]&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2}\\ \frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ G(s)&=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ \frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}&=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ Y(s)&=\frac{1}{s(s+2)}=\frac{1}{2}\left [ \frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+2} \right ] \\ y(t)&=\frac{1}{2}(1-e^{-2t})=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}e^{-2t} \end{aligned}\]

In the following network, the voltage magnitudes at all buses are equal to 1 p.u., the voltage phase angles are very small, and the line resistances are negligible. All the line reactances are equal to \(j1 \Omega\).

If the base impedance and the line-to line base voltage are 100 \(\Omega\) and 100 kV respectively, then the real power in MW delivered by the generator connected at the slack bus is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} P_1&=0.1 \;p.u.\\ &=0.1 \times \frac{(100 kV)^2}{100}\\ &=10MW \end{aligned}\]
